outcome: incidence and distribution of birth-related subdural hemorrhage
presence of other intracranial hemorrhages and associated injuries
sequential evolution of signal changes of birth-related hemorrhages on MRI
cohort: The study included 200 healthy term neonates and young infants, aged 0-2 months, who underwent MRI of the brain and cervical spine.
finding: Birth-related subdural hemorrhage was detected in 33% of healthy term neonates, predominantly in the posterior fossa, showing a characteristic evolution of signal changes on MRI and not persisting beyond 25 days of age, without features concerning for traumatic etiology.
mod_finding: The incidence of subdural hemorrhage was significantly higher in vaginal deliveries (43.9%) compared to cesarean sections (11.8%), with the highest incidence observed in assisted vaginal deliveries (63.3%).
